Q1: Hydrazine's hazard profile indicates known, significant hazards across most categories, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental impacts (ENV), inhalation (IHL), oral (ORL), dermal and eye (SKN), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN), all classified as Tier 1. The only area lacking sufficient data for a confident assessment is endocrine disruption (EDC), which is classified as Tier 4.
Q2: This chemical is recognized on several significant 'Lists of Concern', reflecting its established hazardous nature. It is listed under California's Proposition 65 for causing cancer and reproductive harm, identified as a Hazardous Air Pollutant, and classified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) as a Group 2A carcinogen, meaning it is probably carcinogenic to humans.
Q3: Hydrazine is a very well-characterized chemical, supported by an extensive body of research with 49,000 literature references, significantly higher than the typical chemical. Its molecular formula (H4N2) is precise, and it is classified as a 'Small Molecule,' indicating a well-defined structure. Furthermore, only one of its hazard classes, endocrine disruption, is considered data deficient (Tier 4), suggesting a largely complete hazard assessment.
